title: Quiet Hours: 44 Track Lofi Game Music Pack
tagline: 44 lofi music tracks for any engine: nine screens at four times of day, MIDI and OGG.
description:
Quiet Hours is a 44 track lofi music pack for any game engine: nine game screens at four times of day, in OGG and MIDI.

It ships 36 full looping pieces, 8 short cues and a drumless version of every full piece, royalty free for commercial games, with four full tracks free on this page.

What is inside

44 tracks · 36 drumless versions · OGG + editable MIDI · 1:06:54 of music, not counting the drumless files

  • Nine screens: menu, home, garden, workshop, market, map, reading, rain and waiting. Each one four times: morning (100 BPM), afternoon (86 BPM), evening (74 BPM) and night (60 BPM). The rain pieces are written for a rainy screen and carry no rain sound.
  • One clock per time of day. All nine pieces of a row share one tempo and one loop, so their LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH tags match to the sample, and every track is levelled to -22 LUFS. Start two together, one muted, and fade between them on the same beat. A whole row loaded into one AudioStreamSynchronized in Godot 4.7.2, a test that read the streams and played nothing; in another engine, how tightly they stay together depends on that engine's audio.
  • One scale per time of day. Every note of a row is one of the same seven, so a fade between two of its pieces adds no note from outside them, and each row is one note away from the next. Two pieces may still be on different chords while they overlap.
  • A drumless version of every full piece, same loop tags, same gain, for a dialog box or a quiet moment.
  • Every loop runs at least 96 seconds, the music is low passed at 9 kHz, and the drums are five sounds with no cymbal: kick, side stick, snare, closed hat and shaker.
  • Eight cues for the things that happen in a slow game, among them Alarm Clock, Task Done, Found Something and Wages.
  • One seed theme, Hour, in all 44 tracks, with one more cell for each kind of screen. The keys play third, fifth, seventh and ninth and leave the root to the bass.
  • 26 pitched General MIDI instruments plus two drum kits, among them piano, electric piano, vibraphone, nylon guitar, muted trumpet and kalimba.

The theory and audio reports (784 and 504 checks, 0 failed) and the clock figures for every row ship inside the download.

The grid: every full piece in its cell, with its key, and each row's tempo, loop and scale.

The clock: the nine evening pieces drawn from their MIDI on one time axis, and the seven notes each row uses.

The score sheet: all 44 tracks, from First Light to New Day.

Works with

RPG Maker MV and MZ read the loop tags with no plugin. The Readme gives import steps for Godot 4 (followed in a blank Godot 4.7.2 project, all 44 files), Unity and GameMaker. Any engine that plays OGG can use the files, and the MIDI drops into any DAW.

Try it free

Four full tracks with their MIDI are free on this page, one from each time of day: First Light, Exact Change, Letters to Answer and Quiet Hours. More free tracks from our other albums: Overture, the free sampler.

Licence and how it was made

Royalty free for commercial games, no credit required. Do not resell the tracks as music assets. Every track is composed in code and rendered through a General MIDI soundfont, then low passed, with a written tape wobble in the MIDI and a synthesised hiss and crackle in the OGG files. No generative audio model is used. The composition system and this page's art were made with AI tools, as the tags below say. No song is quoted.

Versions

v1.0 (2 November 2026): first release, 44 tracks.

devlog.title: Quiet Hours is out: a lofi pack with nine screens at four times of day, 44 tracks
devlog.body:
Quiet Hours is a 44 track lofi music pack for games that keep the player on one screen for a long time: menu, home, garden, workshop, market, map, reading, rain and waiting, each at morning, afternoon, evening and night, plus 8 short cues.

The idea. All nine pieces of a time of day share one tempo and one loop to the sample, and every note of that time of day is one of the same seven. So a game can start two of them together, one muted, and fade between them on the same beat, from the home screen to the shop and back. Every full piece also ships without its drums on that same clock.

How it was checked. 784 theory checks and 504 audio checks, 0 failed, with the reports inside the download. The shared loop tags, the seven notes, the drum sounds, the drumless files and the seed theme in every track are measured again on the extracted download. The loop step was followed in a blank Godot 4.7.2 project, and AudioStreamSynchronized loaded a full row and a drumless file there. That test ran with no audio device, so it read the streams and did not play them.

The OGG files are rendered through a General MIDI soundfont, then low passed, with a written tape wobble in the MIDI and a synthesised hiss and crackle in the OGG. Nobody here can hear them: the four free tracks on the page are how to judge the sound. No generative audio model is used. The composition system and the cover art were made with AI tools. No song is quoted.

https://csaf.itch.io/quiet-hours
